title: As if, in a novel
goal: Recognize and use the written as-if forms in -cAsInA, and turn them into everyday gibi.

intro.text: Novels and news say `-cAsInA` where speech says *gibi*: *Hiçbir şey olmamışçasına gülümsedi* (She smiled as if nothing had happened). After the aorist it describes a manner: *koşarcasına* (almost at a run).

vocab.en: burst of laughter (kahkahalarla gülmek: to roar with laughter)
to leap, to dart, to shoot up

exercises.question: Where would you most likely read *Hiçbir şey olmamışçasına gülümsedi*?
options: In a text message to a friend

why.1: In a message to a friend you'd write *olmamış gibi*.

exercises.explain: `-cAsInA` belongs to written narrative. It means the same as `-mIş gibi`.
Aorist *bilir*, then `-cAsInA` with front vowels, and c after the voiced r: *bilircesine*.

exercises.text: Sanki hiçbir şey ___ yoluna devam etti.
exercises.en: She went on her way as if nothing had happened.

reject.why: After the voiceless ş, c becomes ç: *olmamışçasına*.
The suffix follows the back ı of *-mış*: *-çasına*.

accept: She looked at me as if she [were|was] begging.
He looked at me as if he [were|was] begging.
[She|He] looked at me as if begging.

exercises.en: He was walking almost at a run.

exercises.question: Which is the everyday version of *Her şeyi biliyormuşçasına konuşuyor*?

why.1: *Bildiği için* gives a reason: **because he knows**.
why.2: That states two facts; `-cAsInA` only compares.

exercises.explain: `-mIşçAsInA` = `-mIş gibi`: **he talks as if he knew everything**.

accept: The waves were rising as if they were going to swallow the ship.
The waves were rising as if [they would|they were about to|to] swallow the ship.
The waves rose as if [they were going to|they would|they were about to|to] swallow the ship.

exercises.en: Her heart was pounding as if it would leap out of her chest.
exercises.explain: `-(y)AcAkmIşçAsInA`: **as if it were about to**, the written form of *çıkacakmış gibi*.

exercises.prompt: She smiled as if nothing had happened.
exercises.explain: Written: *olmamışçasına*; everyday: *olmamış gibi*. Both are right.

exercises.en: The wind was banging the door as if it would break it.

exercises.task: Rewrite this passage from a novel in everyday spoken Turkish, replacing every `-cAsInA` form with *gibi*.
exercises.source: Adam kapıyı kırarcasına çaldı. Kadın hiçbir şey duymamışçasına okumaya devam etti. Sonra yavaşça kalktı ve sanki bütün dünya onu bekliyormuşçasına kapıya yürüdü.
models: Adam kapıyı kıracak gibi çaldı. Kadın hiçbir şey duymamış gibi okumaya devam etti. Sonra yavaşça kalktı ve sanki bütün dünya onu bekliyormuş gibi kapıya yürüdü.
checklist: Nothing else changes: tenses and word order stay as they are
